items.exampleAf: Ek werk vyf dae per week.
items.exampleEn: I work five days a week.
The bus comes at eight o'clock.

items.exampleAf: My seun is nege jaar oud.
items.exampleEn: My son is nine years old.

items.note: Days are capitalised in Afrikaans.
Days are capitalised in Afrikaans.
Days are capitalised in Afrikaans.
Days are capitalised in Afrikaans.
Days are capitalised in Afrikaans.
Days are capitalised in Afrikaans.

items.exampleEn: On Sunday we go to church.
items.note: Days are capitalised in Afrikaans.

items.exampleAf: Ons ry in April see toe.
items.exampleEn: We go to the sea in April.
We go on holiday in December.

items.note: Also means 'morning'.
Also 'o'clock' (drie-uur = three o'clock).

items.af: Indien die trein twintig minute laat is, mis ons die vergadering.
items.en: If the train is twenty minutes late, we will miss the meeting.
wrongEn: If the train is twelve minutes late, we will miss the meeting.
Although the train is twenty minutes late, we will make the meeting.
Because the train was twenty minutes late, we missed the meeting.
If the train is twenty minutes early, we will miss the meeting.
wrongAf: Indien die trein is twintig minute laat, mis ons die vergadering.
Indien die trein twintig minute laat is, ons mis die vergadering.
Indien die trein twaalf minute laat is, mis ons die vergadering.
Indien die trein twintig minute vroeg is, mis ons die vergadering.
items.note: 'Indien' (if) is formal for 'as'. Its verb goes last (laat is), and the main clause inverts: mis ons.

items.af: Voordat die klok om kwart oor sewe lui, moet almal sit.
items.en: Before the bell rings at quarter past seven, everyone must be seated.
wrongEn: Before the bell rings at quarter to seven, everyone must be seated.
After the bell rings at quarter past seven, everyone must be seated.
Before the bell rings at quarter past seven, nobody may sit.
Before the bell rang at quarter past seven, everyone was seated.
wrongAf: Voordat die klok om kwart oor sewe lui, almal moet sit.
Voordat lui die klok om kwart oor sewe, moet almal sit.
Voordat die klok om kwart voor sewe lui, moet almal sit.
Nadat die klok om kwart oor sewe lui, moet almal sit.
items.note: 'Voordat' (before) sends 'lui' to the end. Kwart oor sewe = 7:15; kwart voor sewe = 6:45.

items.af: Die horlosie wat Oupa my op my sestiende gegee het, loop nog.
items.en: The watch Grandpa gave me on my sixteenth birthday still works.
wrongEn: The watch I gave Grandpa on his sixteenth birthday still works.
The watch Grandpa gave me on my sixth birthday still works.
The watch Grandpa gave me on my sixteenth birthday has stopped.
The watch Grandpa gave me on my sixtieth birthday still works.
wrongAf: Die horlosie wat Oupa my op my sestiende het gegee, loop nog.
Die horlosie wat Oupa my op my sestiende gegee het, loop nie meer nie.
Die horlosie wat ek Oupa op sy sestiende gegee het, loop nog.
Die horlosie wat Oupa my op my sesde gegee het, loop nog.
items.note: The relative clause 'wat ... gegee het' ends with its verbs, then a comma and the main verb: loop. Ordinal: sestiende.

items.af: Die wedstryd is weens reën van Saterdag na Woensdag uitgestel.
items.en: Because of rain, the match was postponed from Saturday to Wednesday.
wrongEn: Because of rain, the match was moved from Wednesday to Saturday.
Because of rain, the match is being postponed to Wednesday.
Despite the rain, the match was played on Saturday.
Because of rain, the match was postponed from Sunday to Wednesday.
wrongAf: Die wedstryd word weens reën van Saterdag na Woensdag uitgestel.
Die wedstryd is weens reën van Saterdag na Woensdag geuitstel.
Die wedstryd het weens reën van Saterdag na Woensdag uitgestel.
Die wedstryd is weens reën van Sondag na Woensdag uitgestel.
items.note: Past passive: is uitgestel (was postponed). Separable uitstel puts ge- in the middle: uitgestel.

items.af: Juffrou het aangekondig dat die toets na die vyftiende verskuif is.
items.en: The teacher announced that the test had been moved to the 15th.
wrongEn: The teacher announced that the test had been moved from the 15th.
The teacher asked whether the test could be moved to the 15th.
The teacher announced that the test had been moved to the 5th.
The teacher announced that the test had been moved to the 16th.
wrongAf: Juffrou het aangekondig dat die toets is na die vyftiende verskuif.
Juffrou het aangekondig dat die toets na die vyftiende geverskuif is.
Juffrou het gevra of die toets na die vyftiende verskuif kan word.
Juffrou het aangekondig dat die toets na die vyfde verskuif is.
items.note: Reported statement with 'dat' plus a passive: verskuif is goes last. Ver- verbs take no ge-. Juffrou = the (female) teacher.

items.af: My suster wou weet hoe laat die bus Saterdag vertrek.
items.en: My sister wanted to know what time the bus leaves on Saturday.
wrongEn: My sister wanted to know what time the bus arrives on Saturday.
My sister told me what time the bus leaves on Saturday.
My sister wanted to know what time the bus leaves on Sunday.
I wanted to know from my sister when the bus leaves on Saturday.
wrongAf: My suster wou weet hoe laat vertrek die bus Saterdag.
My suster wou weet hoe laat die bus Saterdag aankom.
My suster het gesê hoe laat die bus Saterdag vertrek.
My suster wou weet hoe laat die bus Sondag vertrek.
items.note: Reported questions with 'hoe laat' (what time) use statement order: the verb goes to the end.

items.af: Daar is geen bus wat Sondae ry nie, dus moet jy 'n taxi kry.
items.en: There is no bus that runs on Sundays, so you must get a taxi.
wrongEn: There is a bus that runs on Sundays, so you needn't get a taxi.
There is no bus that runs on Saturdays, so you must get a taxi.
There is no taxi that runs on Sundays, so you must get a bus.
There is no bus that runs on Sundays, so you mustn't get a taxi.
wrongAf: Daar is geen bus wat Sondae ry, dus moet jy 'n taxi kry.
Daar is geen bus wat Sondae ry nie, dus jy moet 'n taxi kry.
Daar is geen bus wat ry Sondae nie, dus moet jy 'n taxi kry.
Daar is 'n bus wat Sondae ry, dus hoef jy nie 'n taxi te kry nie.
items.note: 'Geen ... nie' (no ...): the 'nie' comes after the relative clause. 'Dus' (so) is followed by the verb.

items.af: Ek het ure lank gesoek, maar my dagboek was nêrens te vinde nie.
items.en: I searched for hours, but my diary was nowhere to be found.
wrongEn: I searched for hours and finally found my diary.
I searched for a day, but my diary was nowhere to be found.
I searched for hours, but my diary was where I had left it.
I searched for hours, but my appointments weren't in my diary.
wrongAf: Ek het ure lank gesoek, maar my dagboek was nêrens te vinde.
Ek het ure lank gesoek, maar my dagboek was nie nêrens te vinde nie.
Ek het ure lank soek, maar my dagboek was nêrens te vinde nie.
Ek het ure lank gesoek en my dagboek uiteindelik gevind.
items.note: 'Nêrens ... nie' = nowhere. Don't add a second 'nie' before 'nêrens'; it already carries the negation.

items.af: Die eerste keer het ek die marathon in net onder vier uur voltooi.
items.en: The first time, I finished the marathon in just under four hours.
wrongEn: The first time, I finished the marathon in just over four hours.
The first time, I finished the marathon at just before four o'clock.
The last time, I finished the marathon in just under four hours.
Next time I will finish the marathon in under four hours.
wrongAf: Die eerste keer ek het die marathon in net onder vier uur voltooi.
Die eerste keer het ek die marathon in net onder vier uur gevoltooi.
Die eerste keer het ek die marathon in net onder vieruur voltooi.
Die laaste keer het ek die marathon in net oor vier uur voltooi.
items.note: vier uur (apart) = four hours; vieruur (one word) = four o'clock. Voltooi takes no ge- (stress on -tooi).

items.af: Omdat Oupa om vyfuur opstaan, gaan hy met die hoenders slaap.
items.en: Because Grandpa gets up at five, he goes to bed very early.
wrongEn: Because Grandpa gets up at five, he sleeps with the chickens.
Because Grandpa goes to bed very early, he gets up at five.
Because Grandpa gets up at four, he goes to bed very early.
Although Grandpa gets up at five, he goes to bed very late.
wrongAf: Omdat Oupa om vyfuur opstaan, hy gaan met die hoenders slaap.
Omdat Oupa staan om vyfuur op, gaan hy met die hoenders slaap.
Omdat Oupa met die hoenders gaan slaap, staan hy om vyfuur op.
Omdat Oupa om vieruur opstaan, gaan hy met die hoenders slaap.
items.note: 'Met die hoenders gaan slaap' = to go to bed very early (literally: go to sleep with the chickens).

items.af: Die horlosie het die minute stadig afgetel, asof dit ons wou terg.
items.en: The clock slowly counted down the minutes, as if to tease us.
wrongEn: The clock quickly counted down the minutes, as if to help us.
We slowly counted down the minutes, as if to tease the clock.
The clock slowly counted down the hours, because it hated us.
The clock stopped during the last minutes, as if to tease us.
wrongAf: Die horlosie het die minute stadig afgetel, asof dit wou ons terg.
Die horlosie het die minute stadig geaftel, asof dit ons wou terg.
Die horlosie het die minute vinnig afgetel, asof dit ons wou help.
Ons het die minute stadig afgetel, asof ons die horlosie wou terg.
items.note: Personification (verpersoonliking): the clock acts like a person. 'Asof' (as if) sends the verbs last.

items.af: Op die twee-en-twintigste vier my ouers hulle dertigste troudag.
items.en: On the twenty-second my parents celebrate their thirtieth anniversary.
wrongEn: On the twelfth my parents celebrate their thirtieth anniversary.
On the 22nd my parents celebrate their thirteenth anniversary.
On the 22nd my parents celebrated their thirtieth anniversary.
On the second my parents celebrate their thirtieth anniversary.
wrongAf: Op die twee-en-twintigste my ouers vier hulle dertigste troudag.
Op die twee-en-twintigste vier my ouers hulle dertiende troudag.
Op die twaalfde vier my ouers hulle dertigste troudag.
Op die twee-en-twintig vier my ouers hulle dertigste troudag.
items.note: A date placed first pushes the verb before the subject: vier my ouers. Ordinals: twee-en-twintigste, dertigste. Troudag = wedding anniversary.

items.af: As ons gisteraand vroeër vertrek het, sou ons nie die begin van die fliek gemis het nie.
items.en: If we had left earlier last night, we would not have missed the start of the film.
wrongEn: If we had left later last night, we would not have missed the start of the film.
Because we left earlier last night, we did not miss the start of the film.
If we had left earlier last night, we would have missed the start of the film.
If we leave earlier tonight, we will not miss the start of the film.
wrongAf: As ons gisteraand vroeër vertrek het, ons sou nie die begin van die fliek gemis het nie.
As ons gisteraand vroeër het vertrek, sou ons nie die begin van die fliek gemis het nie.
As ons gisteraand vroeër vertrek het, sou ons nie die begin van die fliek gemis het.
Omdat ons gisteraand vroeër vertrek het, het ons nie die begin van die fliek gemis nie.
items.note: Unreal past: as ... het, sou ... het (if we had ..., we would have ...). Negated, it still ends with 'nie'.

items.af: Die begroting, wat in Maart goedgekeur sou word, is weens onenigheid tot Junie uitgestel.
items.en: The budget, which was to be approved in March, was put off until June over disagreement.
wrongEn: The budget, which was approved in March, was put off until June over disagreement.
The budget, which was to be approved in June, was brought forward to March.
The budget, due in March, was approved in June despite disagreement.
The budget, which was to be approved in March, was put off until July.
wrongAf: Die begroting, wat in Maart goedgekeur sou word, het weens onenigheid tot Junie uitgestel.
Die begroting, wat in Maart goedgekeur sou word, is weens onenigheid tot Junie geuitstel.
Die begroting, wat in Maart gegoedkeur sou word, is weens onenigheid tot Junie uitgestel.
Die begroting, wat in Maart goedgekeur is, is weens onenigheid tot Junie uitgestel.
items.note: Two passives: goedgekeur sou word (was to be approved) and is uitgestel (was postponed).

items.af: Die stiptelikheid waarop ons treine eens trots was, het plek gemaak vir vertragings.
items.en: The punctuality our trains were once proud of has given way to delays.
wrongEn: The delays our trains were once ashamed of have given way to punctuality.
The punctuality our trains are still proud of has reduced the delays.
The punctuality our trains were once proud of will give way to delays.
The speed our trains were once proud of has given way to delays.
wrongAf: Die stiptelikheid waarvan ons treine eens trots was, het plek gemaak vir vertragings.
Die stiptelikheid waarop ons treine was eens trots, het plek gemaak vir vertragings.
Die stiptelikheid waarop ons treine eens trots was, het plek maak vir vertragings.
Die stiptelikheid waarop ons treine nog trots is, het die vertragings verminder.
items.note: 'Trots op' (proud of) becomes 'waarop' in a relative clause. 'Plek maak vir' = give way to.

items.af: Die woordvoerder het ontken dat die rooster sonder oorlegpleging ingestel is.
items.en: The spokesperson denied that the roster had been introduced without consultation.
wrongEn: The spokesperson admitted that the roster had been introduced without consultation.
The spokesperson denied that the roster had been introduced after consultation.
The union denied that the roster had been introduced without consultation.
The spokesperson denied that the roster would be introduced without consultation.
wrongAf: Die woordvoerder het ontken dat die rooster is sonder oorlegpleging ingestel.
Die woordvoerder het geontken dat die rooster sonder oorlegpleging ingestel is.
Die woordvoerder het erken dat die rooster sonder oorlegpleging ingestel is.
Die vakbond het ontken dat die rooster sonder oorlegpleging ingestel is.
items.note: Reported denial with a passive: dat ... ingestel is. Ont- verbs take no ge-: ontken. Separable instel: ingestel.

items.af: Hy skuif alles op die lange baan, en gevolglik moes hy gisteraand tot middernag werk.
items.en: He puts everything off, and consequently he had to work until midnight last night.
wrongEn: He pushes everything onto the long track, so he had to work until midnight.
He does everything early, so he could go to bed before midnight last night.
He puts everything off, but last night he still went to bed early.
He never puts anything off, yet he had to work until midnight last night.
wrongAf: Hy skuif alles op die lange baan, en gevolglik hy moes gisteraand tot middernag werk.
Hy skuif alles op die lange baan, en gevolglik moes hy gisteraand tot middernag gewerk.
Hy skuif alles op die kort baan, en gevolglik moes hy gisteraand tot middernag werk.
Hy doen alles betyds, en gevolglik kon hy gisteraand voor middernag gaan slaap.
items.note: 'Iets op die lange baan skuif' = to put something off. 'Gevolglik' (consequently) is followed by the verb: moes hy.

items.af: Die tyd is 'n rivier wat niemand kan keer nie: dit spoel ons jare verby.
items.en: Time is a river that nobody can stop: it washes our years past.
wrongEn: Time is a river that everybody can stop: it washes our years past.
A river that nobody could stop washed our years away.
Time is a river that nobody can cross: it washes our years past.
Time is a river that nobody can stop: it washed our house away.
wrongAf: Die tyd is 'n rivier wat niemand kan keer: dit spoel ons jare verby.
Die tyd is 'n rivier wat niemand keer kan nie: dit spoel ons jare verby.
Die tyd is 'n rivier wat niemand kan keer nie: dit verbyspoel ons jare.
Die tyd is 'n rivier wat niemand kan oorsteek nie: dit spoel ons jare verby.
items.note: An extended metaphor: time IS a river. The separable verb verbyspoel splits in a main clause: spoel ... verby.

items.af: Nooit tevore is soveel deelnemers op een dag ingeskryf nie: meer as vierduisend!
items.en: Never before had so many entrants been registered in one day: over four thousand!
wrongEn: Never before had so few entrants been registered in one day: under four hundred!
So many entrants are often registered in one day: over four thousand!
Never before had so many entrants been registered in one day: over 14,000!
Never before had so many entrants been registered in one day: over four hundred!
wrongAf: Nooit tevore soveel deelnemers is op een dag ingeskryf nie: meer as vierduisend!
Nooit tevore is soveel deelnemers op een dag ingeskryf: meer as vierduisend!
Nooit tevore is soveel deelnemers op een dag geinskryf nie: meer as vierduisend!
Nooit tevore is soveel deelnemers op een dag ingeskryf nie: meer as vierhonderd!
items.note: 'Nooit tevore' (never before) placed first forces inversion (is soveel deelnemers) and still needs 'nie'.

items.af: Hoewel die verskuiwing van die sperdatum verligting gebring het, het almal steeds gewag.
items.en: Although moving the deadline brought relief, everyone still waited.
wrongEn: Because moving the deadline brought relief, everyone finished early.
Although moving the deadline caused stress, everyone still waited.
Although moving the deadline brought relief, nobody waited.
Although the deadline was not moved, everyone still waited.
wrongAf: Hoewel die verskuiwing van die sperdatum verligting het gebring, het almal steeds gewag.
Hoewel die verskuiwing van die sperdatum verligting gebring het, almal het steeds gewag.
Hoewel die verskuiwing van die sperdatum verligting gebring het, het almal steeds wag.
Omdat die verskuiwing van die sperdatum verligting gebring het, was almal vroeg klaar.
items.note: A nominalisation (die verskuiwing = the moving) as subject inside a 'hoewel' clause; verbs go last.
